_note: "What This Book Argues" claims model — the SSOT for the six headline claims named on book/frontmatter/0.2-what-this-book-argues.md. These are the book's ARGUMENT (the six things the chapters set out to convince you of), distinct from claims_declared.json (which holds the 19 finer discussion-level claims the spine reconciles against) and from landing-big-ideas.json (the six Big Ideas rendered on the site landing). Kept as its own registry because several Part-opener foreshadows trace to an argument PREMISE that maps to no Big Idea — a premise headlines the argument here even when it is not a landing slot. Each key is a stable slug; `id` is the `argues-<slug>` node id; `order` mirrors the on-page 1-6 order; `statement` is the claim's bold headline plus its one-line gloss. Consumed by book-models/lint_part_opener_traceability.py: leg (c) of the traceability loop closes when a foreshadowed spine node reconciles to a Big Idea OR to one of these argument-claims (the ids appear as `reconciles.argues_claims` slugs in argument_spine_declared.json). No site projection — a pure lint-consumed registry, mirroring the brick-fitness.json genre.

cheap-code-costly-judgment.statement: Commodity intelligence changes the economics of software engineering. Implementation capacity is becoming abundant relative to engineering judgment. As that constraint loosens, engineering effort shifts toward what remains scarce: deciding what should be built, representing the system well enough to reason about it, producing evidence, and giving consequential intent authority.

se-is-long-horizon-reasoning.statement: Scale creates a reasoning problem. Large software systems already exceed the reasoning horizon of humans; agents inherit the same problem. Software engineering has always answered scale with abstraction. Commodity intelligence does not remove that need. It makes the quality of the representations through which work proceeds increasingly consequential.

models-help-reason.statement: The Modeling Thesis. Externalize engineering knowledge and intent into explicit, purposeful models that preserve what an engineering question needs and suppress what it does not. Models let humans and agents reason about larger properties without repeatedly reconstructing them from implementation, and they make more consequential facts available to tools.

reliability-from-environment.statement: The Alignment Thesis. Give engineering obligations authority through constraints, sensors, validators, and gates embedded in the engineering environment. Alignment does not require a comprehensive model of the system: a sandbox, a test, or a permission boundary can already hold a local rule. Explicit models expand what can be stated and checked deterministically; where the necessary abstraction is absent, human judgment often fills the gap.

every-failure-becomes-infrastructure.statement: Governance conversion turns recurring judgment into engineering capital. When a failure exposes missing knowledge or an unenforced obligation, encode the lesson into durable engineering structure. The immediate repair fixes one instance; conversion reduces the cost of the next change by preventing the same judgment from being repeatedly rediscovered.

engineers-role-changes.statement: The profession changes. Engineers increasingly design the representations, evidence, policies, and governed environments through which abundant implementation capacity can be used safely. Writing implementation remains engineering work; it is no longer where all of the leverage resides.
